name: Vo 2 max
seoDesc: Vo 2 max: work out age from the resting heart rate and the walk time. A free sports calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The Vo 2 max calculator turns the resting heart rate, the walk time and the pulse into age. Think of it as a shortcut for a training session, a performance comparison or a competition result. Every field is labelled the way you would say it out loud, so you can usually fill the form from memory and only look up the numbers you genuinely do not know.

sections.title: How does the Vo 2 max calculator work?
sections.html:
The Vo 2 max calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports age in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the method, the sex and the training level); then you type in the resting heart rate, the walk time, the pulse (Personal data) and the pulse (Personal data).

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Vo 2 max calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Age=2080 ÷ 7 − 10 ÷ 7 × max heart rate m1
Vo 2 max=((51 ÷ 10) × max heart rate m1 ÷ resting heart rate)
Vo 2 max=(-3877 ÷ 10000 × age − 939 ÷ 1000 × pulse − 32649 ÷ 10000 × walk time − 769 ÷ 10000 × weight + 17396 ÷ 125)
Vo 2 max=(-3877 ÷ 10000 × age − 939 ÷ 1000 × pulse − 32649 ÷ 10000 × walk time − 769 ÷ 10000 × weight + 132853 ÷ 1000)
Vo 2 max=(11133 ÷ 100 − 42 ÷ 25 × pulse)
Vo 2 max=(6581 ÷ 100 − 1847 ÷ 2500 × pulse)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Suppose Method set to Resting heart rate, Sex set to Male, Resting heart rate = 10 and Walk time = 10 hrs. Working through the relationship above gives Vo 2 max = 58.

The point of the example is the scale, not the particular digits: swap in your own figures and the same relationship produces your answer.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Vo 2 max = 58 should be roughly the size you expected from Method set to Resting heart rate and Sex set to Male.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Time, opening in minutes / seconds

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Vo 2 max calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Tracking progress across a training block
  • Planning a session around a target you already know
  • Comparing two athletes or two attempts fairly
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the resting heart rate, the walk time and the pulse — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Vo 2 max calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns age, derived from the resting heart rate, the walk time and the pulse. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Vo 2 max calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the resting heart rate, the walk time and the pulse, which is 11 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter weight in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Weight opens in kilograms and the chip beside it offers 29 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (3 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Vo 2 max = 58. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Vo 2 max calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
